SUMMARY: Epic 22 - Post-release backlog
DESCRIPTION: Everything still open after the epics 8-21 release (2026-10-05), from the retro Backlogs, ranked by risk: P1 production risk and data correctness, P2 personal data in the database (decision C), P3 feature gaps, P4 polish. Build order and sources: epic-22-build-order.md.

SUMMARY: Saved templates belong to a user, in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my saved templates to be mine and to follow me to other devices, so nobody else on this browser sees them.
DESCRIPTION: ledger_transaction_templates (useTransactionTemplates.ts) is one local-storage key with no user scope: anyone who signs in on the same browser sees the previous user's templates (LED-189 backlog; decision C, 2026-10-05). Move them to a transaction_templates table (id, user_id, name, values jsonb, created_at) with RLS on user_id. First load uploads the browser's templates once when the table has none for the user, then removes the key. Sign-out clears any local copy. Migration must reach production before the client (release checklist B).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Migration applies to an empty database in CI and has RLS (own rows only); (b) a second user on the same browser sees none of the first user's templates; (c) templates created on one device appear on another; (d) existing browser templates are uploaded once, not duplicated on a second load; (e) sign-out leaves no template key in local storage; (f) Cookies and storage notice row updated (wording approved by the owner, OD-5); (g) release checklist lists the migration.

SUMMARY: Errors reach the operator, not only the console
USER_STORY: As the operator, I want to know when Ledger fails for a user, so I can fix it without waiting for a report.
DESCRIPTION: Every caught error and error boundary logs to the browser console only (LED-243 backlog: "No error reporting service"). Decide the sink first: (a) a hosted tracker such as Sentry (new outbound host: CSP and Privacy Policy change together, see patterns/outbound-host-needs-csp.md and OD-9); (b) an error_events table in Supabase written through RLS; (c) keep console only. Then route ErrorBoundary, WidgetErrorBoundary and unhandled rejections to it, without amounts, descriptions or other personal data.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Owner picks a sink; (b) a forced error in production appears in it with route, release sha and browser, and no financial data; (c) for (a), the CSP header and Privacy Policy name the host (wording approved, OD-5); (d) local dev does not report.

SUMMARY: CSP blocks a blob: worker
USER_STORY: As a user, I want every part of Ledger to work under its security policy, so nothing fails silently.
DESCRIPTION: The epics 15-19 phase 3 sweep saw "Creating a worker from 'blob:...' violates ... worker-src 'self'" in the console; never investigated. Find what creates the worker (PWA service worker, a chart or CSV library), whether production shows it (https://ledger-personal.vercel.app), and what breaks. Either allow blob: in worker-src in vercel.json and index.html together, or stop the library creating one.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The source is named in the retro; (b) production console shows no CSP violation on Home, Activity, Reports and Import; (c) if the policy changes, vercel.json and the index.html meta still differ only as release checklist C3 allows; (d) live check after deploy.

SUMMARY: A renamed recurring row does not post a back-dated duplicate
USER_STORY: As a user, I want renaming a recurring transaction to leave its schedule alone.
DESCRIPTION: LED-232's backfill grouped series by description. An older row renamed apart from its series is unmatched and can post one back-dated row the first time any device runs the generator; a series that missed its post while another series under the same description posted later can be marked wrongly (LED-232 retro backlog). Check whether production has any such rows (read-only query), then key the series on something stable (source id or a series id) instead of the description.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Read-only query run on production, count in the retro; (b) renaming a recurring row and reloading posts nothing extra (local, two devices); (c) tests for the series key; (d) no change to rows already posted.

SUMMARY: Splitting a posted recurring row does not post it again
USER_STORY: As a user, I want splitting a recurring transaction to keep one schedule, not one per line.
DESCRIPTION: split_transaction gives each line is_recurring with recurrence_next_posted false, so splitting a row that already posted its next occurrence makes each line post its own next date (LED-232 retro backlog). Decide: lines are not recurring (the source keeps the schedule), or the flag is carried to every line.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Splitting a recurring row that already posted, then loading the app, posts nothing; (b) the next due date posts once; (c) migration (if the RPC changes) applies cleanly in CI; (d) test or SQL check in the retro.

SUMMARY: An offline edit of a recurring row does not report a false conflict
USER_STORY: As a user, I want an offline edit to sync quietly when nobody else changed the row.
DESCRIPTION: post_recurring_transaction updates the source row's recurrence_next_posted, which bumps updated_at. A queued offline edit of that same row then reports a conflict when it drains, though only the generator touched it (LED-232 retro backlog, not verified in the browser). Verify, then compare conflicts on user-visible fields only, or keep updated_at for the flag update.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Reproduced or ruled out in the browser; (b) if real: edit a recurring row offline, let the generator post, reconnect: the edit applies without a conflict; (c) a real concurrent edit of the same field still reports one.

SUMMARY: Preferences live in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my number and date format and list settings on every device.
DESCRIPTION: ledger-preferences (usePreferences.ts): number locale, date format, large-transaction threshold, card notifications, transaction view and density, account view and group order. Move to profiles.preferences jsonb with defaults; local copy is a cache. One-time upload when the column is empty. Decision C, 2026-10-05.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Migration with default and RLS through profiles; (b) a change on one device shows on another after reload; (c) first load uploads existing browser preferences once; (d) offline, the local copy is used and the change syncs later or is reported.

SUMMARY: Which Home widgets show lives in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my Home layout the same on every device.
DESCRIPTION: Widget order is already profiles.dashboard_widget_order; which widgets are hidden is only ledger-dashboard-widgets in the browser (useDashboardPrefs.ts). Add profiles.dashboard_hidden_widgets, upload once, drop the local key and the now-redundant local order key.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Hiding a widget on one device hides it on another; (b) existing browser state uploaded once; (c) both local keys gone after migration.

SUMMARY: The setup checklist state lives in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a dismissed setup checklist to stay dismissed on a new device.
DESCRIPTION: ledger-first-run (useFirstRunChecklist.ts) holds whether the pay cycle was confirmed and whether the checklist was dismissed. Move to profiles columns; upload once.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Dismissed on one device stays dismissed on another; (b) pay cycle confirmation follows the user; (c) existing state uploaded once.

SUMMARY: Card reminders already shown live in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a card reminder once, not once per device.
DESCRIPTION: <userId>:cc-notifs-sent (useCreditCardNotifications.ts) records which reminders were shown, per browser. Move to profiles.card_reminders_sent jsonb (or a small table), pruned of past statements.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A reminder shown on one device is not shown again on another; (b) the stored list does not grow without bound; (c) existing state uploaded once.

SUMMARY: 13th Month picks live in the database
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my 13th Month picks on every device.
DESCRIPTION: 13th-month-selection:<userId>:<year> (ThirteenthMonthPage.tsx) per browser. Move to a thirteenth_month_picks table (user_id, year, transaction ids) with RLS; upload once.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Picks made on one device show on another; (b) a deleted transaction drops out of the picks; (c) existing picks uploaded once.

SUMMARY: Sign-out clears personal browser copies; the storage notice says "kept in your account"
USER_STORY: As a user, I want signing out to leave none of my data in this browser.
DESCRIPTION: After LED-257 and LED-263 to LED-267, sign-out clears their local caches; theme, text size and accent stay per device (decision C). Update STORAGE_ROWS and the Cookies and storage notice: each moved group reads as kept in your account, cleared from this browser at sign-out. Legal wording: the owner approves before commit (OD-5).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) After sign-out, local storage holds only appearance, the install-banner flag and other sites' keys; (b) notice wording approved before commit; (c) tests/legalPages and browserStorage tests pass; (d) the Privacy Policy agrees.

SUMMARY: Card and loan payments, and imported transfers, between two currencies
USER_STORY: As a user who pays a card or loan from an account in another currency, I want the amount received recorded.
DESCRIPTION: LED-185 added destination_amount for manual transfers only. cardPaymentTransfer forces rate 1 with no destination amount, and importTransfer.ts offers same-currency targets only (LED-185 retro backlog). Extend the amount-received field to card payments and loan repayments, and let an import match a cross-currency transfer.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A card paid from a different-currency account asks for the amount received and moves both balances correctly; (b) same for a loan repayment; (c) an import can link a cross-currency transfer; (d) statements and loan schedules use the received amount.

SUMMARY: Import cannot make a plain transfer into a credit card
USER_STORY: As a user importing a statement, I want a card payment recorded as a card payment.
DESCRIPTION: The import's transfer picker offers a credit card as a target (LED-188 sweep, not checked). A card payment has its own rules (rules/card-payment-is-a-transfer.md: statement and payment history). Check what an imported transfer into a card does today; then route it through the card-payment path or leave cards out of the picker.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Behaviour today recorded in the retro; (b) an imported payment to a card updates the statement and payment history like a manual one, or cards are not offered; (c) test for the picker.

SUMMARY: Overspending weekly and quarterly rows drop the "1st" streak
USER_STORY: As a user, I want the Overspending streak to mean something for every budget period.
DESCRIPTION: Weekly and quarterly budgets in Overspending show a meaningless "1st" streak, and their window is not the pay cycle (LED-244 backlog; outside OD-13's scope).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Weekly and quarterly rows show no streak, or a streak counted in their own periods; (b) monthly and yearly rows unchanged; (c) tests.

SUMMARY: Pay now on an overdue loan bill dates the payment today
USER_STORY: As a user paying an overdue installment, I want the payment dated when I pay it.
DESCRIPTION: Pay now on a loan bill whose due date is past opens the repayment form dated on the old due date (LED-145 retro backlog).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Pay now on an overdue bill opens dated today; (b) on an upcoming bill, behaviour unchanged (decide: today or due date) and recorded.

SUMMARY: Screen-reader leftovers
USER_STORY: As a screen-reader user, I want every control named and every change announced.
DESCRIPTION: From the LED-179 tree pass: the palette opens with the first option highlighted but no aria-activedescendant until an arrow press; Activity's search input is named by its placeholder only; "Nothing is waiting." after the last queue discard is not announced.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Palette announces the highlighted option on open; (b) Activity search has an accessible name; (c) the empty queue state is announced politely; (d) checked in the accessibility tree.

SUMMARY: Home detail pane and account side column match the design widths
USER_STORY: As a user on a wide screen, I want the panes at their designed size.
DESCRIPTION: Home's docked detail pane is 340px (DashboardDetailSurface.tsx) against 400 in 17a; the account page's side column is 320px at every width against 400 in 4a at 1920 (epics 15-19 phase 4 backlog, LED-209). Measure each before changing it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Measured against 17a and 4a at 1280 and 1920; (b) widths changed only where the design and the content agree; (c) no horizontal scroll at 1280.

SUMMARY: Skeleton loading bars are visible in light mode
USER_STORY: As a user on the light theme, I want to see that something is loading.
DESCRIPTION: Grey skeleton runs on a white card are faint in light mode; the tokens were not changed (epics 15-19 phase 3 backlog).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Skeleton contrast against the card at least 1.5:1 in light (decorative, not text); (b) dark unchanged; (c) tokens only, no per-component colours.

SUMMARY: Link preview image in the current brand
USER_STORY: As the owner, I want a shared link to look like today's Ledger.
DESCRIPTION: public/social-preview.svg/.png are the pre-redesign beige card; the app is now the dark "L." brand. Design decision first; then render the PNG from the new SVG with headless Chrome at 1200x630, as in the og:image change of 2026-10-05.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Owner approves a design; (b) PNG 1200x630 under 300 KB; (c) live check: og:image and twitter:image load on https://ledger-personal.vercel.app.
